Turn a pipeline into a function

Source: R/as_function.R
as.function.pipeflow.Rd

Returns a function that runs a copy of the pipeline x and returns the output of selected steps. The function arguments are the unbound parameters of x, with their current values as defaults. As any other function, it can be added to an "outer" pipeline with pip_add(), in which case the unbound parameters of x become parameters of that pipeline. To bind parameters of x to output of steps of the outer pipeline, pass them as references in params of pip_add(), e.g. pip_add(outer, "inner", f_inner, params = list(df = ~outer_step)).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'pipeflow'
as.function(
  x,
  out = NULL,
  cache = TRUE,
  on_error = c("stop", "continue"),
  lgr = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A pipeflow pipeline (not a view; use x[i, view = FALSE] to turn a part of a pipeline into a function).

out

The result of the function. NULL (the default) returns the outputs of all steps as a named list, see pip_collect(); a step name returns the output of that step; several step names return a named list of their outputs. A function with at least one argument is called with (a light copy of) the run inner pipeline and returns the result, see Details.

cache

Whether to keep the run copies of x for reuse, TRUE (the default) or FALSE. The function keeps one copy per outer step and partition, see Details.

on_error

What to do when an inner step fails: "stop" (the default) ends the inner run at that step, "continue" runs the inner steps that do not depend on it, see Details and pip_run().

lgr

The logger of the inner run, see pip_run(). NULL (the default) runs the inner pipeline silently. To activate logging, set e.g. lgr = pipeflow_lgr.

...

Not used.

Value

A function with the unbound params of x as arguments.

Details

By default, the inner pipeline is run silently, but warnings and messages of its steps are still passed on to the caller. A failing inner step results in an error of the caller which in turn makes the outer step fail. Param values of the outer pipeline reach the function unwrapped (see pip_param_value()). The arguments of the function are values, also if they are formulas: unlike in pip_set_params(), a formula argument does not bind a param of x to a step.

Choosing the output

With step names in out, the function returns their outputs. If out is a function, it is called with the run inner pipeline, and its result is the result of the function, e.g. out = \(p) pip_collect(p, by = "tags") groups the outputs by tags. The pipeline that out gets is a light copy of the kept one: it has its own steps, but the values (params and outputs) are the same objects. Returning it, or a view of it, therefore keeps no extra copy of the data, and later calls of the function don't change it. Since the values are shared, don't modify them in place (e.g. with := on a data.table output).

Continuing after errors of inner steps

With on_error = "continue" the inner pipeline is run like pip_run(on_error = "continue"), that is, a failing inner step gets state "failed", the inner steps that do not depend on it still run, and an inner step that refers to it via ~try(step) runs and receives the failure.

The function still fails if one of the steps named in out failed or was not run because an input failed. Since with out = NULL or a function out all steps are requested, you need to name the relevant steps in out to profit from a continuing inner run.

Pipeline functions with partitioned inputs

If the step with the pipeline function receives partitioned inputs (from an earlier step with exec = "split"), the function is called once per partition caching one inner pipeline of x per step and partition key. A call updates its parameters and inputs in the respective pipeline, so that (as usual in pipelines) only outdated inner steps are run again. This works for inputs bound via params of pip_add() as well as for those bound in the step function.

  • A partition caches one pipeline for each key, which hold their inputs and outputs, so they need memory.

  • A step without partitioned inputs keeps a single pipeline.

  • Pure calls of the pipeline function (outside of a step) always share one pipeline, e.g. lapply(subsets, f_pip) don't cache anything.

  • Do not use the same pipeline function in two different pipelines - this avoids name clash of keys, which would prevent proper caching (not wrong but slower).

  • Cached pipelines are stored in the function. If you save the function or send it to another process, they are copied, including their data and output, so new runs work independently from the original. A function that has not been called yet, or one made with cache = FALSE, has no pipelines and therefore is small to copy.

  • In case of an error, the error message includes the key of the partition and the name of the failed inner step.

Limits

  • Params that several steps of x share by name become one argument, with the default of the first step as in pip_get_params(). Every call sets this value in all of these steps, so a step whose own default differs from it runs with the value of the argument.

  • Inputs are compared as they are. A change made in place to an environment or another reference object (e.g. R6) is not seen: as for pip_set_params() of a pipeline, which needs force = TRUE, the steps stay up to date. A forced run of the outer pipeline (pip_run(force = TRUE)) does not force the inner pipelines either, but you can force them by setting cache = FALSE.

Note

The conversion is done by taking a snapshot of x. Later changes of x therefore don't have an impact on the function. Also all steps start as new, so the pipeline function result does not depend on whether x has been run before, except for locked steps, which keep their outputs.

See also

pip_add(), pip_inner() to look at the kept inner pipelines

Examples

inner <- pip_new("inner") |>
  pip_add("input", \(input_df = NULL) input_df) |>
  pip_add("fit", \(data = ~input, degree = 1) {
    lm(mpg ~ poly(wt, degree, raw = TRUE), data = data)
  }) |>
  pip_add("coefs", \(fit = ~fit, digits = 2) round(coef(fit), digits))

# As a plain function: the unbound params are its arguments
f_inner <- as.function(inner, out = "coefs")
f_inner(input_df = mtcars, digits = 1)
#>                  (Intercept) poly(wt, degree, raw = TRUE) 
#>                         37.3                         -5.3 

# As a step: one inner pipeline
single <- pip_new("single") |>
  pip_add("df", \(df = mtcars) df) |>
  pip_add("coefs", f_inner, params = list(input_df = ~df))

pip_run(single, lgr = NULL)
single[["coefs", "out"]]
#>                  (Intercept) poly(wt, degree, raw = TRUE) 
#>                        37.29                        -5.34 

# Only the inner steps after the changed param run again
pip_set_params(single, list(digits = 3))
pip_run(single, lgr = NULL)
single[["coefs", "out"]]
#>                  (Intercept) poly(wt, degree, raw = TRUE) 
#>                       37.285                       -5.344 

# With partioned inputs: one inner pipeline per cylinder number
outer <- pip_new("outer") |>
  pip_add("df", \(df = mtcars) df) |>
  pip_add("by_cyl", \(df = ~df) split(df, df$cyl), exec = "split") |>
  pip_add(
    "coefs",
    as.function(inner, out = "coefs"),
    params = list(input_df = ~by_cyl)
  ) |>
  pip_add("table", \(coefs = ~coefs) do.call(rbind, coefs), exec = "reduce")

pip_get_params(outer)

pip_run(outer, lgr = NULL)
outer[["table", "out"]]

#> 4       39.57                        -5.65
#> 6       28.41                        -2.78
#> 8       23.87                        -2.19

# Only the steps after the changed param run again, for each partition
pip_set_params(outer, list(digits = 3))
print(outer)
#> <pipeflow> outer (4 steps)
#> --------------------------
#>      step                 params depends    state                 out   exec
#> 1:     df                     df             done <data.frame[32x11]>   auto
#> 2: by_cyl                     df      df     done           <list[3]>  split

#> 4:  table                  coefs   coefs outdated       <matrix[3x2]> reduce

pip_run(outer, lgr = NULL)
outer[["table", "out"]]
#>   (Intercept) poly(wt, degree, raw = TRUE)
#> 4      39.571                       -5.647
#> 6      28.409                       -2.780
#> 8      23.868                       -2.192

# Don't use the same function for the same step name in two pipelines:
# this breaks the caching (results are still correct, but it is slower)
a <- pip_new("a") |>
  pip_add("df", \(df = mtcars) df) |>
  pip_add("coefs", f_inner, params = list(input_df = ~df))
b <- pip_new("b") |>
  pip_add("df", \(df = mtcars[mtcars$am == 1, ]) df) |>
  pip_add("coefs", f_inner, params = list(input_df = ~df))

pip_run(a, lgr = NULL)
pip_run(b, lgr = NULL)

# The inner pipeline now holds the input of `b`, so all its steps run again
# for `a`, not only the ones after `digits`
pip_set_params(a, list(digits = 3))
pip_run(a, lgr = NULL)
a[["coefs", "out"]]
#>                  (Intercept) poly(wt, degree, raw = TRUE) 
#>                       37.285                       -5.344 

# Better: make one function per pipeline
pip_replace(
  a, "coefs", as.function(inner, out = "coefs"),
  params = list(input_df = ~df)
)

# A function as out: the outputs grouped by tags
tagged <- pip_new("tagged") |>
  pip_add("input", \(input_df = NULL) input_df) |>
  pip_add("n", \(data = ~input) nrow(data), tags = "summary") |>
  pip_add("mpg", \(data = ~input) mean(data$mpg), tags = "summary") |>
  pip_add("fit", \(data = ~input) lm(mpg ~ wt, data = data), tags = "model")

f_tagged <- as.function(tagged, out = \(p) pip_collect(p, by = "tags"))
res <- f_tagged(input_df = mtcars)
names(res)
#> [1] "summary" "model"  
res$summary
#> $n
#> [1] 32
#> 
#> $mpg
#> [1] 20.09062
#> 

# With on_error = "continue", the inner pipeline handles a failed inner
# step itself: `coefs` is run with the failure of `fit` and reports it.
robust <- pip_new("robust") |>
  pip_add("input", \(input_df = NULL) input_df) |>
  pip_add("fit", \(data = ~input) {
    if (nrow(data) < 3) stop("too few rows to fit")
    lm(mpg ~ wt, data = data)
  }) |>
  pip_add("coefs", \(fit = ~try(fit), digits = 2) {
    if (inherits(fit, "pipeflow_failure")) NULL else round(coef(fit), digits)
  })

f_robust <- as.function(robust, out = "coefs", on_error = "continue")
f_robust(input_df = mtcars)
#> (Intercept)          wt 
#>       37.29       -5.34 

# the continued inner run signals a warning instead of an error
suppressWarnings(f_robust(input_df = mtcars[1:2, ]))
#> NULL
